messages.subject: methRead function change the chromosome ID
parts:
Hi,
I am using the fucntion methRead() to read input files, and to create a methylDB.
When i checked methylRawListDB object I realized that the chromosome ID column had been changed.
``̀`
the head of the file test1-TechRep_1-BioRep_1.deduplicated.CX_report.txt
Chr15 4 + 0 0 CHH CCC
Chr15 5 + 0 0 CHH CCT
Chr15 6 + 0 0 CHH CTA
Chr15 11 + 0 0 CHH CCC
Chr15 12 + 0 0 CHH CCT
Chr15 13 + 0 0 CHH CTA
Chr15 18 + 0 0 CHH CCC
Chr15 19 + 0 0 CHH CCT
Chr15 20 + 0 0 CHH CTA
Chr15 25 + 0 0 CHH CTA
``̀`
``̀`
library("methylKit")

file.list1 = list("/test1-TechRep_1-BioRep_1.deduplicated.CX_report.txt",
                 "/test2-TechRep_1-BioRep_2.deduplicated.CX_report.txt",
                 "/ctrl1-TechRep_1-BioRep_3.deduplicated.CX_report.txt",
                 "/ctrl2-TechRep_1-BioRep_2.deduplicated.CX_report.txt")


readingReports1=methRead(file.list,
                        sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),
                        assembly="bismark",
                        treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
                        context="CpG",
                        mincov = 10,
                        pipeline= "bismarkCytosineReport",
                        dbtype = "tabix",
                        dbdir = "methylDB"
)

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: methRead function change the chromosome ID
parts:
Hi Fatima,

Based on what you show I think there are two things happening here:
The head on the orignal file shows many lines with CHH context, which is not the one that you selected, thus they are ignored. 
The second thing is that the original ordering will not preserved, but you can check which chromosomes remain using something like table(getData(object)$chr).

Best,
Alex
